stem: Study the given diagrams. In the first, two masses \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) are separated by a distance \(d\); in the second, the same masses are separated by a distance \(3d\). If in the first case \(F = \dfrac{Gm_1m_2}{d^2}\), then find the force \(F\) in the second case.
solution: In the second case the separation is \(3d\), so \(F = \dfrac{Gm_1m_2}{(3d)^2} = \dfrac{Gm_1m_2}{9d^2}\).

subtopic: Early Attempts and Mendeleev's Periodic Table
stem: In the Dobereiner's triad Li, Na, K, the atomic masses of lithium and potassium are 6.9 and 39.1 respectively. What will be the atomic mass of sodium?
solution: According to Dobereiner's law of triads, the atomic mass of the middle element (Na) is the average of the atomic masses of Li and K. Atomic mass of Na \(= \dfrac{6.9 + 39.1}{2} = 23\).

stem: State whether the given statement is true or false: A concave lens is a converging lens.
solution: False. A concave lens is a diverging lens.

stem: Find the odd man out: Tinning, Anodization, Alloying, Froth flotation.
solution: Froth flotation. Tinning, anodization and alloying are processes of coating/protecting the surface of metals (corrosion prevention), whereas froth flotation is a method of concentration (separation) of ore.

stem: The reaction of iron nail with copper sulphate solution is ________ reaction.
solution: The reaction of an iron nail with copper sulphate solution is a displacement reaction (iron displaces copper from copper sulphate).

stem: Observe the given diagram (set-up A: resistors \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) connected in series across a 5 V cell; set-up B: resistors \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) connected in parallel), which shows the magnetic lines of force produced, and choose the correct alternative:

options.label: A
options.text: The intensity of magnetic field in A is larger than in B.

options.label: B

options.label: C

solution: In set-up A the resistors are in series (higher total resistance, smaller current), while in set-up B they are in parallel (lower total resistance, larger current). A larger current produces a stronger magnetic field, so the intensity of the magnetic field in A is less than in B.

stem: A ray of light makes an angle of \(50^\circ\) with the surface \(S_1\) of the glass slab. Its angle of incidence will be ________.
solution: The angle of incidence is measured from the normal (perpendicular) to the surface. Since the ray makes \(50^\circ\) with the surface, the angle of incidence \(= 90^\circ - 50^\circ = 40^\circ\).

stem: Water expands on reducing its temperature below ________ \(^\circ C\).
solution: Water shows anomalous expansion — it expands on cooling below \(4\,^\circ C\).

stem: The carbon compound used in daily life is ________.
solution: Edible oil is a carbon compound used in daily life.

stem: Two tungsten bulbs of power 50 W and 60 W work on 220 V potential difference. If they are connected in parallel, how much current will flow in the main conductor?
solution: For bulbs in parallel, \(I = I_1 + I_2 = \dfrac{P_1}{V} + \dfrac{P_2}{V} = \dfrac{P_1 + P_2}{V} = \dfrac{50 + 60}{220} = \dfrac{110}{220} = 0.5\ \text{A}\). A current of 0.5 A will flow through the main conductor.

stem: Give scientific reason: In electric equipment producing heat, e.g. iron, electric heater, boiler, toaster etc., an alloy such as Nichrome is used, not pure metals.
solution: The working of such equipment is based on the heating effect of electric current. An alloy such as nichrome has high resistivity and can be heated to a high temperature without oxidation. Hence nichrome, and not a pure metal, is used in heat-producing equipment such as the iron, electric heater, boiler and toaster.

subtopic: Free Fall and Acceleration due to Gravity
stem: A metal ball of mass 5 kg falls from a height of 490 m. How much time will it take to reach the ground? \((g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2)\)
solution: Given \(u = 0\), \(a = g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\), \(s = 490\ \text{m}\). Using \(s = ut + \tfrac{1}{2}at^2\): \(490 = 0 + \tfrac{1}{2}\times 9.8 \times t^2\), so \(t^2 = \dfrac{490}{4.9} = 100\) and \(t = 10\ \text{s}\). The time required is 10 s.

subtopic: Free Fall and Acceleration due to Gravity
stem: What would be the value of 'g' on the surface of the earth if its mass were twice and its radius half of what it is now?
solution: We know \(g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}\). Given \(M_2 = 2M_1\) and \(R_2 = \tfrac{1}{2}R_1\). Then \(\dfrac{g_2}{g_1} = \dfrac{M_2}{M_1}\times\dfrac{R_1^2}{R_2^2} = \dfrac{2M_1}{M_1}\times\dfrac{R_1^2}{\left(\tfrac{1}{2}R_1\right)^2} = 2\times 4 = 8\). So \(g_2 = 8g_1\); the value of 'g' becomes eight times its present value.

subtopic: Early Attempts and Mendeleev's Periodic Table
stem: Write the merits of Mendeleev's periodic table.
solution: Merits of Mendeleev's periodic table: (i) To give elements their proper place in accordance with their properties, the atomic masses of some elements were revised. (ii) Mendeleev kept vacant places in the table for elements not discovered till then; when these elements were later discovered, their properties matched well with those predicted by Mendeleev. (iii) Although there was no place reserved for noble gases originally, when noble gases such as helium, neon and argon were discovered, Mendeleev created a 'zero' group without disturbing the original table, in which the noble gases fitted very well.

subtopic: Latent Heat and Change of State
stem: Explain the given temperature vs time graph (with points A, B, C, D) showing the changes occurring when a mixture of ice and water is heated.
solution: The graph shows the changes occurring when a mixture of ice and water is heated. Along the line AB the temperature of the mixture remains constant till all the ice melts — this constant temperature is the melting point of ice (0 \(^\circ C\)). On further heating, the temperature rises steadily from 0 \(^\circ C\) to 100 \(^\circ C\), shown by the line BC. At 100 \(^\circ C\) (point C) water starts converting to steam — this is the boiling point of water. Along the line CD further heating does not change the temperature.
figureNote: Temperature (°C) vs time (minutes) graph for heating an ice + water mixture: flat segment AB near 0°C (ice + water / solid + liquid), rising segment BC from 0°C to 100°C (water / liquid, liquid-gaseous state), flat segment CD at 100°C (boiling water + vapour) (page 4, Q3(4)).

stem: What is meant by space debris? Why is there a need to manage the debris?
solution: Non-functional satellites, parts of launchers detached during launching, and debris generated due to collisions between satellites or other objects in space comprise space debris. This debris can be harmful to artificial satellites — it can collide with satellites or spacecraft and damage them. Because this debris is increasing day by day, it will become difficult to launch new spacecraft in the future. Therefore it is essential to manage space debris.

stem: Why is this arrangement of elements similar to the above period of the modern periodic table?
solution: On moving from left to right within a period, the atomic number increases by one and the positive charge on the nucleus increases by one unit, but the electrons are added to the same orbit (shell). Therefore the nuclear pull increases and the atomic size decreases — giving the same decreasing order of atomic radius as observed across the period.

stem: Draw the diagrams of the three observations made by Swarali.
solution: Three diagrams at a denser-rarer (denser below, rarer above) boundary, with the normal shown: (a) angle of incidence i less than the critical angle — the refracted ray bends away from the normal into the rarer medium (with a weak partially reflected ray); (b) i equal to the critical angle — the refracted ray grazes along the boundary (angle of refraction = 90�\(^\circ\)); (c) i greater than the critical angle — no refraction; the ray undergoes total internal reflection and returns into the denser medium (angle of reflection r' = i).
